question: What is the primary clinical goal of emergency wound management?

options.A: Covering the defect with tight bandages
options.D: Restoring tissue integrity and preventing infection

explanation: Emergency wound care focuses primarily on closing the defect properly while keeping bacteria out to ensure optimal healing. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why does the time since an injury happen matter when treating a wound?

options.A: Wounds older than twelve hours have a much higher infection risk
options.B: Sutures dissolve faster if placed too late
options.C: Local anesthetics stop working effectively after six hours
options.D: Skin elasticity decreases rapidly within the first hour

explanation: Bacteria multiply significantly over time in open tissue, making delayed primary closure safer for older wounds. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h1)

question: Which local anesthetic agent is most commonly used for emergency wound suturing?
explanation: Lignocaine provides rapid and reliable local nerve blockade for minor surgical procedures in the emergency setting. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h2)

question: Where should you avoid injecting local anesthetic mixed with adrenaline?
explanation: Adrenaline causes vasoconstriction which can cut off blood supply entirely in end-arterial digits, leading to tissue death. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the main reason for cleaning out and removing tissue from a wound before closing it?

options.A: Enlarging the incision for better visibility
options.B: Diluting bacterial load with sterile water

explanation: Debridement clears away non-viable tissue that would otherwise support bacterial growth and delay proper healing. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h3)

question: Why is gentle washing preferred over high-pressure spraying for dirty wounds?

options.A: It activates the local anesthetic solution more effectively
options.B: It ensures the sterile saline warms up to body temperature
options.C: It reduces the total volume of fluid required for the procedure
options.D: It prevents driving bacteria deeper into the underlying tissue

explanation: Excessive pressure during irrigation can force surface contaminants further into microscopic tissue planes, worsening the infection risk. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which type of thread is non-absorbable and usually chosen for closing skin cuts?
explanation: Nylon is a non-absorbable synthetic polymer that elicits minimal tissue reaction and is standard for skin surface closure. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h4)

question: Why do nurses and doctors use a cutting needle when stitching up a skin cut?

options.A: It prevents the suture thread from fraying under tension
options.B: It dissolves safely inside the subcutaneous fat layer
options.C: It easily penetrates tough, fibrous dermal tissue
options.D: It eliminates the need for administering local anesthesia

explanation: Skin is a tough, fibrous organ; a cutting needle has a built-in blade edge that smoothly slices a path through it. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h4)

question: What is the main benefit of using simple interrupted stitches?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for subcutaneous stitches
options.B: If one stitch fails, the remaining sutures keep the wound secure
options.C: It is the fastest method to close very long lacerations
options.D: It requires fewer instruments than any other closure method

explanation: Because each stitch is tied separately, a localized complication or failure will not compromise the entire wound closure. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h5)

question: Which stitching method works best to make sure the skin edges roll slightly outward?
explanation: The vertical mattress technique incorporates deep and superficial bites that naturally flip the skin edges outward, preventing depressed scars. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h5)

question: About how many days after stitching should facial skin sutures be removed?
explanation: Facial skin heals rapidly and has a rich blood supply, so sutures are removed early to prevent permanent cross-hatch marks. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h6)

question: Which symptom is most characteristic of an early surgical site infection?

options.A: Clear serous fluid draining within the first hour
options.B: Spreading erythema and warmth around the wound edges
options.C: Temporary numbness directly beneath the repaired skin
options.D: Mild itching sensation during the third week of healing

explanation: Progressive redness, heat, and throbbing pain indicate bacterial proliferation requiring prompt clinical re-evaluation. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T3#GNS311_U4_T3_h6)
